title: Vanishing Walsh character sum for a nonzero index
statement:
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $z$ be an $n$-bit Boolean input that is $\mathrm{true}$ in at least one coordinate, say $z_i = \mathrm{true}$ for some index $i$. For a Boolean input $x$, write $\langle x, z\rangle = \bigoplus_{j} (x_j \wedge z_j)$ for their mod-2 inner product, and let $s(x) \in \{\pm 1\}$ be the sign $+1$ when $\langle x, z\rangle$ is $\mathrm{false}$ and $-1$ when it is $\mathrm{true}$. Then summing this sign over all $2^n$ Boolean inputs $x$ gives
\[
  \sum_{x} s(x) = 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: z is an n-bit Boolean input
z has some coordinate i with z_i = true
replaced:
If $z : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ has a coordinate $i$ with $z_i = \mathtt{true}$, then
\[
  \sum_{x : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n} \mathrm{boolSign}(\mathrm{innerProduct}(n, x, z)) = 0.
\]
This is the orthogonality of Walsh characters for the inner product function.
